note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: Big Tech wants to tap Wall Street's big wallets
items.blurb: AI capex is outgrowing corporate cash flow, pushing hyperscalers toward debt and asset-manager financing.

items.title: Google's new AI boss inherits a race to catch OpenAI and Anthropic
items.blurb: Koray Kavukcuoglu takes day-to-day control of Google DeepMind from Demis Hassabis, with Gemini 3.5 Pro still unshipped.

items.title: Anthropic's text watermarks signal new front in AI detection
items.blurb: Anthropic marks Claude output with text watermarks and file metadata worldwide, meeting the EU AI Act's Aug 2 rule.

items.title: Meta and Nvidia plant 'very firm flag' in open-weight AI race led by Chinese labs
items.blurb: Muse Glimmer and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning test whether US open weights can win users from DeepSeek, Qwen and Moonshot.

items.title: AI's costly buildout complicates the Fed's inflation fight
items.blurb: Data-center spending is pushing up power and component prices, muddying the inflation picture policymakers must read.

items.title: CoreWeave surges 18% in premarket after a 'cleaner quarter'
items.blurb: The AI cloud provider's results are read as a demand signal for rented frontier-model training and inference capacity.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: Chips, ships and a sliding yen
items.blurb: Markets slipped as investors weighed concentrated AI revenue and the financing behind the compute buildout.

items.title: AI agents' 'alarming' hacking skills creates rush to spend on cybersecurity
items.blurb: Gartner sees information-security spending rising 12.5% to $240 billion in 2026 as agentic attacks compress intrusions into seconds.

items.title: The push to create a futures market for AI compute
items.blurb: Trading compute like oil or grain would add price transparency and hedging to AI's scarcest and costliest input.

items.title: Huge pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic to continue spending as they head toward listings
items.blurb: Analyst argues both labs must sustain capex to justify pre-IPO valuations, tightening the loop between spending and listings.

items.title: A clinically validated framework for auditing AI chatbot behavior in mental health interactions
items.blurb: Across 810 simulated conversations, frontier chatbots often amplified psychiatric vulnerabilities; newer models scored better but risks persisted.

items.title: AI brings savings to clinical trials: study
items.blurb: Tufts analysis finds AI agents cut roughly 10 weeks and up to $5.6M from late-stage cancer drug trials.

items.title: Google's new Pixel 11 puts Gemini at center of AI phone battle with Apple
items.blurb: Google ships its most agentic Gemini on Pixel 11 weeks before Apple launches a Siri built on the same models.

items.title: Wall Street just endorsed Jensen Huang's 'big concept' for AI. What now?
items.blurb: Six asset managers backing Nvidia's plan treat AI compute as a financeable asset class, not a depreciating capex line.

items.title: Why Intel's selling new stock
items.blurb: Intel is issuing equity into a 150% year-to-date run, funding fab expansion off AI-driven chip demand.

items.title: Manus to return as independent company after China forced Meta to unwind $2 billion deal
items.blurb: Chinese regulators unwound Meta's agent-startup acquisition, showing Beijing will block outbound AI deals on national grounds.

items.title: AI computing power is becoming a tradable asset class as CME launches futures contracts
items.blurb: CME and Silicon Data will list two compute futures contracts Oct 5, pending approval, turning GPU rental cost into a hedgeable price.

items.title: OpenAI executive Brad Lightcap is leaving
items.blurb: Another early OpenAI leader departs, continuing a pattern of senior staff leaving frontier labs to start their own ventures.

items.title: Memory chip prices are skyrocketing. Here's why they will stay high.
items.blurb: Hyperscalers are locking up memory supply years ahead, squeezing PC and phone makers and pushing consumer hardware costs up.

items.title: New York Post launches "Hamilton" AI chatbot
items.blurb: A major newsroom ships Gemini-powered search, briefings and recommendations, testing how far publishers will hand personalization to models.

items.title: CoreWeave stock pops 14% as revenue doubles on accelerating AI infrastructure demand
items.blurb: Revenue up 112% year over year, a live read on how fast rented AI compute is still selling.

items.title: Why Jensen Huang's $500 billion AI financing plan faces a big risk from China
items.blurb: Nvidia's vendor-financing push depends on demand that export controls and Chinese substitution could undercut.

items.title: Nvidia's AI revolution will be securitized
items.blurb: Six asset managers would turn GPU purchases into structured debt, making chips a tradable credit product.

items.title: Security leaders are stuck in decision paralysis over AI-enabled cyberattacks
items.blurb: CrowdStrike reports an 89% rise in attacks using AI, while defenders stall on which tools to adopt.
